solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The anger when cleaner breaks this piece of apparatus

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one word breaks another when it splits it open and sits in the middle

parts.note: to anger someone is to rile them
a mop is a cleaning implement

explanation.surface: A cleaner damaging a delicate instrument in the lab provokes fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anger' is a verb here, not a noun; 'when' and 'this' are only link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermopile is an instrument made of linked thermocouples that measures radiant heat, so it is a piece of scientific apparatus.

clue.text: Tenor with good sense of music!

definitions.text: Tenor with good sense of music!

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for tenor in vocal music
someone with an ear for music has a good sense of it

explanation.surface: Praise for a singer whose musical instinct is spot on.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: Robert Tear was a distinguished Welsh tenor, and a tenor with a good ear is exactly what the wordplay builds.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Tear was a celebrated Welsh operatic tenor, so the surname fits a singer praised for musicality.

clue.text: Win a vase, from what they say

indicators.note: signals that the word for a vase is to be heard, not read, giving a soundalike

parts.note: an urn is a kind of vase

explanation.surface: Someone hears they have won a vase as a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn something is to win or gain it through effort.

clue.text: Sketch makes mother pull a face

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
to pout is to pull a sulky face

explanation.surface: A child's drawing makes their mother grimace.
explanation.definitionFit: To map out a plan is to sketch it in outline.

clue.text: Medical practitioner, quietly I stop hysteria spreading around hospital

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the letter for hospital
hysteria that spreads is scattered about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A doctor tries to calm panic sweeping through a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' rearranges ISTOPHYSTERIA and 'around' places H within it, after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A physiotherapist is a health professional who treats injury by exercise and massage, so a practitioner of medicine.

clue.text: Monkey showing fatigue, not getting round

indicators.note: says a piece is left out of the word for fatigue

parts.note: languor is weariness or lethargy
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A tired monkey that cannot manage another lap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not getting' removes O (round) from LANGUOR; 'showing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The langur is a long-tailed leaf-eating monkey of South Asia.

clue.text: Old rodent seen around plant

indicators.note: turning something around reverses it, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: An elderly rat is spotted near some vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen around' reverses ORAT as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Taro is a tropical plant grown for its starchy edible root.

clue.text: A very small insect on ground by house, lacking tail and not boringly normal?

parts.note: taken as written
an ant is a small insect

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a garden is the ground beside a house

explanation.surface: A tiny bug in a garden seems surprisingly unconventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking tail' cuts the last N from GARDEN. The definition's question mark marks a playful description rather than a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Avant-garde art is experimental and innovative, the opposite of the dull mainstream.

clue.text: Fair sited in an area of flat land

definitions.meaning: honest or straightforward, as a fair dealer is

definitions.text: sited in an area of flat land
definitions.meaning: literally placed on ground that is level

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means honest and genuine, and literally it means situated on level ground.

clue.text: Mistreated a pony — girth is shrinking

indicators.note: something mistreated is knocked about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A badly handled pony's girth is getting smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mistreated' rearranges APONYGIRTH; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To atrophy is to waste away, so a muscle atrophying is shrinking.

clue.text: Long underwear to be cut short

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

parts.note: pants are underwear

explanation.surface: Long johns being trimmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the S of PANTS; 'to be' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To pant for something is to long for it eagerly.

clue.text: Cooked meat served in special basket, note

indicators.note: read as something specially made up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dish served in a fancy basket with a note attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges BASKETNOTE; 'served in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bone steak is a cut of beef with a T-shaped bone, usually grilled.

clue.text: Outlandish description of Humpty after accident

definitions.meaning: Humpty Dumpty in the nursery rhyme sat on a wall and had a great fall, ending up away from it

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means bizarre or unconventional, and literally describes the egg-shaped Humpty having fallen from his perch.

clue.text: Call promises of payback 'suspect'

parts.note: to dub someone is to call or name them
IOUs are written promises to repay a debt

explanation.surface: Someone calls a set of debt promises questionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubious and suspect both mean doubtful or not to be trusted.

clue.text: Important contest — journalist turns up with drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the letters backwards

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is a crossword journalist
cider is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A reporter arrives with a drink before a big match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses ED to DE.
explanation.definitionFit: A decider is the final game that settles a tied series, so an important contest.

clue.text: Grand vessel with a green colour

parts.note: a sub (submarine) is a vessel
lime is a shade of green

explanation.surface: A fine boat painted a bright green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sublime means awe-inspiring or exalted, as does grand.

clue.text: Cafeteria is hit

definitions.meaning: a self-service food counter or refreshment room
is struck repeatedly, as by wind or waves

explanation.definitionFit: A buffet is a self-service eating place, and to be buffeted is to be struck repeatedly.

clue.text: Whisper when saint breaks law

indicators.note: one word breaks into another by splitting it open

parts.note: a rule is a law

explanation.surface: Quiet murmuring as a holy figure transgresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' looks like law-breaking in the surface but signals the insertion; 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustle is a soft whispering sound, as of leaves.

clue.text: Get into all-night dancing somewhere in London

indicators.note: letters that dance move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An invitation to an all-night party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges GETINTOALLNIGHT. NOTTING HILL GATE is a district and Tube station in west London, close to the famous carnival.
explanation.definitionFit: Notting Hill Gate is an area and Underground station in west London.

clue.text: Pin in end of frock picked by seamstress?

indicators.note: the letter is taken in by, so put inside, the following word

parts.note: a seamstress is one who sews, a sewer; the question mark flags the pun

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A pin is spotted in the hem of a dress by a dressmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked by' puts K inside SEWER, read as 'one who sews' rather than a drain. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A skewer is a long pin used to hold meat together while cooking.

clue.text: Garment right for concealing British criminal

indicators.note: the outer letters hide the next piece inside them

parts.note: a robe is a garment

explanation.surface: A thief hides a British criminal under a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for concealing' puts B inside ROBER.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber is a criminal who steals by force.

clue.text: Soil say turning to mire after start of September

indicators.note: the following pieces come after the opening letter
the reversed piece is added to the word for mire
takes the first letter of the word

parts.note: mire is mud

indicators.note: the letters are read backwards

parts.note: EG (for example) is what 'say' means in a clue

explanation.surface: Wet ground turns boggy as September begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses EG to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To smudge is to soil or smear something.

clue.text: Fights for morsels of food

explanation.definitionFit: Scraps are both minor fights and small leftover pieces of food.

clue.text: Glamour brought by Catholic to Church of England

parts.note: Roman, as in Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: A Catholic brings some sparkle to the Anglican church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought by' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Romance is a quality of glamour and excitement or mystery.

clue.text: Cheese omelette finally produced by mother

indicators.note: takes the last letter of the word

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A mother makes a cheese omelette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced by' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese.

clue.text: Small bird, one in shrub in US

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A little bird perches in an American bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. The bird is not the definition: the answer is also an evergreen shrub of the southern US.
explanation.definitionFit: Titi is a flowering evergreen shrub found in the southeastern United States.

clue.text: Problem with erstwhile commentator John on the radio

indicators.note: signals a soundalike, while also nodding at Snagge's radio career

parts.note: John Snagge was a BBC radio commentator and newsreader

explanation.surface: Trouble involving a former broadcaster on air.
explanation.walkthrough: John Snagge was a famous BBC radio voice, known for commentating the Boat Race.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is an unexpected problem or obstacle.

clue.text: Duty of American soldier seen in retrospect in sacrifice

indicators.note: places the reversed piece inside the word for sacrifice

parts.note: an oblation is an offering or sacrifice

indicators.note: looking back means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A US soldier's duty of sacrifice, looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in retrospect' looks like a time phrase but means read backwards, and 'in' then signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: An obligation is a duty one is bound to perform.

clue.text: Do away with expertise, not requiring leader

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: skill is expertise

explanation.surface: Getting rid of know-how without needing a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill is to do away with someone.

clue.text: Priest not awfully good kicking up a fuss?

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman who is anything but good causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges PRIESTNOT, then G is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Protesting is objecting loudly, which is kicking up a fuss.
